notes: The road east is three small plans with one short window each, joined by hard cuts; the plain beat carries the design note's two big wides, Asher and the jenny tiny on the road and the city lit across the plain.

Kallias's court at night is one stitched long take from the gate to the spilled silver (W04 to W23), the camera passing between diners, cups and faces at couch height, the design note's signature move for Scene 7.

By the owner's map instruction the court is a premium Greek peristyle of 26 columns at 2.9 to 3 m bays, with the open stone shrine of Tyche at the east end and the blazing central brazier on the court axis before her; the gate is at the west, so the dawn wind out of the east carries her ash over the sleeping couches.

Kallias, Asher and Philon share the head couch facing the goddess, so Kallias writes at Asher's elbow and Asher's arm reaches Philon's neck; Jes sits on the couch edge in the gap before the low table.
Kallias's two opening blocks share W05 with a pause between them; Asher's two blocks around the tablet sit in W10 and W12, with the silent tablet business in W11.
The camera works the high table from five sides (the gap before the couch, both ends of the table, the far side and behind the couch); inset A shows those paths at large scale.
The beggar's corner is outside the gate on its north side, where the company turns up the street, so in Scene 9 the company passes within arm's reach of it on its way in.
At dawn Kallias and the priest are gone and Philon sleeps at the end of the couch; half asleep, Asher speaks at 2.2 words a second and Jes answers as softly.
The dawn and the gate are hard cuts, a time jump and another night; the gate scene ends on the beggar's empty hand.
The west gate square that the design note lists under Scene 7 sits in the screenplay's #8# section, so Scene 8 stages it.
